cohort: Parturients in Enugu, Nigeria, divided into two groups: those with short IPI (<18 months) and those with normal IPI (>=18 months).
finding: Women with short interpregnancy intervals were more likely to have lower birthweight babies and experience adverse pregnancy outcomes like maternal anaemia, preeclampsia, and caesarean delivery.
birth_weight: 2664.13 +/- 339.25g in women with short IPI vs 3670.63 +/- 452.69g in women with normal IPI
